battle.name: 神風連之亂
battle.brief: 一八七六年十月二十四日深夜，肥後藩士太田黑伴雄、加屋霽堅等約一百七十人結敬神黨，分隊襲擊熊本鎮台司令官種田政明與縣令安岡良亮宅，再攻入熊本城殺傷守兵、占砲兵營。翌晨兒玉源太郎指揮步兵第十三連隊與砲兵第六大隊反攻，首謀者重傷自刃。加特林式機槍日境內僅數門，熊本火線未見其蹤。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 大日本帝國陸軍一方，主力是駐紮熊本城內的熊本鎮台，下轄步兵第十三連隊（連隊長陸軍中佐與倉知實）、砲兵第六大隊，以及熊本縣警察部轄下的第二、第三屯營巡查隊；指揮系統自東京陸軍省而下，經鎮西台所（所長陸軍少將奧保鞏）直達熊本鎮台司令長官（陸軍少將種田政明），亂起後由陸軍少將兒玉源太郎接手指揮。另一方是敬神黨，骨幹是肥後熊本藩的士族、官職下級與神社神職組成的敬神愛護會，結集時約一百七十人，作戰時增至一百七十四至二百餘人，分數隊行動，首領太田黑伴雄，副首領加屋霽堅，另有齋藤求三郎、上野堅五、蓮田善明等人。反對的一方給他們安上「神風連」的貶稱，因熊本一帶把鄉黨組織稱為「連」，言下之意是視之為受排遣的私黨；故正名為敬神黨之亂，通稱神風連之亂。
countriesEn: The Imperial Japanese Army side was centred on the Kumamoto Garrison (Kumamoto chinadai), stationed inside Kumamoto Castle and supervised from the Chinzei Depot (Chinzei daisho) in Kumamoto. Under it stood the 13th Infantry Regiment, commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Tomomichi Yokoura, the 6th Artillery Brigade, and the police detachments (ton'ei) of the Kumamoto Prefectural Police Department under the 2nd and 3rd districts. The chain of command ran from the Army Ministry in Tokyo down through the Chinzei Depot under Major General Yutaka Okubo to the garrison commander, Major General Masaaki Tanda, who was killed on the night; command then passed to Major General Gen'itaro Kodama. The other side was the Keishinto, the party revering the gods: the backbone of the Keishin Aigokai drawn from Higo-Kumamoto samurai, junior officials and shrine priests, who mustered about 170 men and fielded between 174 and a little over 200 on the night, operating in several separate bands. Their leader was Tomoo Otaguro, with Harukata Kaya as deputy, joined by Kyuzabiro Saito, Kengo Ueno and Zenmyo Ren. Their opponents gave them the derogatory nickname Shinpūren, because in the Kumamoto area a local party organisation was called a ren; the implication was that they were a private faction mustered for a plot. Hence the formal name Keishinto no ran, popularly the Shinpūren Rebellion.
people: 敬神黨首謀者太田黑伴雄，天保六年出生於熊本城下町，幼名鐵兵衛，父太田黑惟信時任熊本縣民會議長；他是反對明治政府洋式政策最力的肥後士族之一，一八七六年在熊本策劃起兵，事發夜中彈重傷，退入附近民家後自刃。副首領加屋霽堅是熊本藩士出身、熊本錦山神社（加藤神社）神職，兼敬神黨代表，陣亡於官軍反攻的銃火之下；齋藤求三郎同樣中彈身亡，上野堅五、蓮田善明先後斃命。背後的學術養育來自林櫻園一系在熊本的私塾：林櫻園與河上彥齋兩人已於一八七一年先後病故，未能親與其事，但他們的國學與神道主張構成勤皇黨的精神骨架。官軍方面，熊本鎮台司令長官種田政明少將當夜在自宅遇襲身亡，鎮台參謀長高島茂德中佐亦於襲擊中戰死；縣令安岡良亮在對策會議中受重傷，十月二十七日傷重死亡；縣參事小關敬直重傷，翌年身亡；鎮西台所長奧保鞏在官軍重新集結時居中接應。兒玉源太郎少將連夜趕抵熊本城，在零散中整頓隊伍重新編組，指揮全線反攻，收回砲兵營與武器庫，事後接掌熊本鎮台。步兵第十三連隊少佐林隼之助整頓混亂隊伍、一齊射擊，軍曹幡穐守為奪回武器庫戰死，兵卒隈部幸作奪回被擲出的連隊旗；警察方面，七等警部嶋田弘與屯營巡查津田長鎮、森彌在往來縣廳途中殉職。種田的愛妾小勝從熊本電信局發出「ダンナハイケナイ ワタシハテキズ」的電報，事後成為電報文體的著名範例。
peopleEn: Tomoo Otaguro, born in 1835 in the castle town of Kumamoto, was the leader of the Keishinto; his childhood name was Tetsubei, and his father Kore Nobumi Otaguro, then president of the Kumamoto Prefectural Assembly, was among those attacked and escaped. Otaguro was one of the Higo samurai most sharply opposed to the Meiji government's Westernising policies, and in 1876 he planned the rising in Kumamoto; that night he was hit by a bullet, withdrew into a nearby house and killed himself. His deputy Harukata Kaya, a samurai by birth and priest at Kumamoto's Kin'yama Shrine (now Kato Shrine), who also served as the Keishinto's spokesman, was killed by the returning fire; Kyuzabiro Saito likewise fell, and Kengo Ueno and Zenmyo Ren were killed in turn. The intellectual background came from Rinsuen's private academy in Kumamoto: Lin Sakuraen and Kawakami Kosai had both died of illness in 1871 and never witnessed the event, but their advocacy of kokugaku and Shinto supplied the moral spine of the loyalist faction. On the government side, garrison commander Major General Masaaki Tanda was killed in an attack on his own house on the night, and garrison chief of staff Lieutenant Colonel Shigetoku Takashima also died in the assault. Prefect Yoshiaki Yasuoka was gravely wounded while attending a counter-measures meeting and died of his wounds on 27 October; prefectural councillor Naonobu Kozeki was badly hurt and died the following year. Major General Yutaka Okubo of the Chinzei Depot received the rallying government troops as they re-formed. Major General Gen'itaro Kodama reached Kumamoto Castle during the night, reorganised scattered detachments into order and directed the counter-attack that recovered the artillery camp and the arms store, afterwards taking over the Kumamoto garrison. In the 13th Infantry Regiment, Major Hayanosuke Hayashi brought an undisciplined company into line and fired in unison; Sergeant Ishimori Hatake lost his life fighting to retake the arms store, and a rank-and-file soldier, Kousaku Kumabe, recovered the regimental colour that had been thrown out. On the police side, seventh-class inspector Hiroshi Shimada and district constables Nagachika Tsuda and Yutaka Mori were killed on their way to the prefectural office. Tanda's concubine, who had survived, ran to the Kumamoto telegraph office and sent the message Dan'nai hikenai watashi wa tekizu, which later became a celebrated example of telegraphic economy.
kits: 官軍步兵第十三連隊的制式火器是明治三年定型的十八式小銃，一種前裝轉後膛的單發線膛槍，採金屬藥莢配合布帶的定裝藥包，連隊射擊時不必頻頻分裝，槍身自帶刺刀；砲兵第六大隊配備野戰砲與霰彈砲，砲兵營內另有待發實包與備用炮件，軍中並備有連隊旗一類的指揮標誌。敬神黨一方則是典型的過渡期武裝：舊式洋槍、火繩與雷管皆有的前裝槍支，數量有限而彈藥不足，另有大量冷兵器——因廢刀令禁止帶刀，他們仍把刀佩在身上，夜戰中雙方短兵相接，白刀相交；政府軍傷員的刀創由石黑忠悳所繪《明治九年神風黨刀創圖》逐件記錄。指定的那件兵器加特林機槍，一八六零年前後由美國人理查德·喬丹·加特林研製，一八六一年取得專利，靠人手搖動曲柄讓六根槍管依次旋轉射擊，後坐力分散在六次發射上，因而能以每分鐘二百發的節奏壓制密集隊形；一八六六年美軍正式採用，南北戰爭後期已有少量實戰記錄。它在日本境內的地位極為邊緣：戊辰戰爭期間全國僅存三門，其中兩門由長岡藩藩主河井繼之助自瑞士商行購得，餘下一門裝在幕府自美國購入的裝甲艦甲鐵號上，一八六八年曾傳出用於反擊榎本軍回天丸接舷攻擊。一八七四年四月北海道開拓使自美購得兩挺，同年八月美國總統格蘭特再贈明治天皇一挺，該年臺灣出兵亦留下加特林式機槍實戰投入的記錄，而熊本鎮台正是那次出兵部隊之一。可是在一八七六年十月的熊本火線上，這一型多管機槍並無投入的記載；這場衝突實際是由後膛步槍、野砲與冷兵器近戰分出勝負。
kitsEn: The standard firearm of the government infantry was the 18th Year Type rifle standardised in 1870, a single-shot rifled breechloader converted from the earlier percussion pattern, firing fixed metallic cartridges carried in cloth belts, which let a regiment keep up its rate of fire without stopping to sort loose rounds; bayonets were fixed to the muzzle. The 6th Artillery Brigade was equipped with field guns and shrapnel pieces, and the artillery camp held ready ammunition and spare gun equipment; the army also carried regimental colours as signs of command. The Keishinto's armament was typical of a transitional age: old foreign rifles, some still percussion or even flint, few in number and short of ammunition, together with a great deal of cold steel. Because the edict banning swords had forbidden them to wear blades, they kept their swords anyway, and in the night fighting the two sides closed to short range and crossed blades; the sword cuts sustained by government soldiers were recorded wound by wound in Mitsugu Shigeno's illustrated chart of wounds, Meiji 9 nen Shinto to tosō zu. The designated weapon, the Gatling gun, was developed around 1860 by the American Richard Jordan Gatling and patented in 1861; six barrels are turned by a hand crank so that they fire in turn, and because the recoil is spread over six separate shots it can hold down a dense formation at a rate of about two hundred rounds a minute. It was formally adopted by the US Army in 1866 and saw limited service late in the American Civil War. Its position in Japan was marginal: at the time of the Boshin War only three existed in the country, two of them bought for Nagaoka domain by its lord Tsunesuke Kawai from a Swiss trading house, the third mounted on the ironclad Kotetsu, purchased by the shogunate from America, with a report that it was used in 1868 to answer the boarding attack by the warship Kaiten Maru. In April 1874 the Hokkaido Development Commission bought two from America, in August of that year President Grant presented one more to the Meiji Emperor, and the Taiwan expedition of the same year records the Gatling gun in action, the Kumamoto garrison among the units sent. Yet on the Kumamoto front in October 1876 there is no record of this multi-barrel gun being committed: the fighting was in fact decided by breechloading rifles, field guns and cold steel at close quarters.
tactics: 敬神黨的打法是一場典型的深夜多路同步襲擊：十月二十四日入夜後，各隊同時撲向數處宅邸與官廳——熊本鎮台司令長官種田政明宅、參謀長高島茂德宅、步兵第十三連隊長與倉知實宅、縣民會議長太田黑惟信宅，以及正在召開對策會議的縣令安岡良亮宅——目標不是攻奪陣地，而是精準斬首指揮鏈與縣廳主官，再趁官軍失去統一指揮的混亂，集中攻入熊本城內的鎮台兵舍，逐段殺傷驚覺中的守兵，順利占領砲兵營與鄰近的武器庫。叛軍並無後續計畫：一旦首謀者中彈、指揮中斷，全隊即失去士氣，多數人當場自刃或被俘。官軍的應手完全相反，兒玉源太郎連夜集結潰散隊伍，先重整編制、統一射擊，再分頭奪回砲兵營與武器庫，由少佐林隼之助整頓混亂的連隊並整齊射擊，軍曹幡穐守與兵卒隈部幸作在混戰中分別搶回武器庫與連隊旗。地形上，交火集中在熊本城內外的坡道、濠塹與南坂一帶，坪井川邊亦是潰退與落水之地。通訊方面，電信線已通至九州，熊本電信局成為唯一的報警管道，一封電報即可把事變送到東京。時間上，整場戰鬥自深夜起至翌日清晨結束，十月末的九州夜裡寒氣逼人，雙方在黑暗中多靠喊話、刺刀與槍口焰辨別敵我。
tacticsEn: The Keishinto's method was a classic synchronised night attack by several columns. After nightfall on 24 October the bands struck at once at a number of residences and official buildings: the house of garrison commander Masaaki Tanda, that of chief of staff Shigetoku Takashima, that of 13th Infantry commander Tomomichi Yokoura, that of prefectural assembly president Kore Nobumi Otaguro, and the prefect's residence, where a counter-measures meeting was under way. The aim was not to carry a position but to decapitate the chain of command and the head of the prefectural government; then, exploiting the confusion left by government troops without unified control, they concentrated on the garrison barracks inside Kumamoto Castle, killing the alerted garrison in sections, and seized the artillery camp and the neighbouring arms store. The rebels had no plan for the aftermath: once the leader was hit and command broke down, the whole band lost heart, and many killed themselves on the spot or were captured. The government's reply was the exact opposite. Kodama Gen'itaro gathered the scattered troops during the night, first restored order and unit identity and unified the fire, then moved in parallel to retake the artillery camp and the arms store. Major Hayanosuke Hayashi straightened out the confused company and fired in unison, while Sergeant Ishimori Hatake and the soldier Kousaku Kumabe fought their way back to the arms store and the colours in the melee. The fighting was concentrated on the slopes, ditches and the southern rampart around Kumamoto Castle, and the Tsukui River was where men were driven back and drowned. For communications, the telegraph line already reached Kyushu, and the Kumamoto telegraph office became the only channel for raising the alarm, a single message carrying the news to Tokyo. In time, the whole fight ran from late night to the following morning, a matter of some hours; the nights in Kyushu were cold by late October, and in the darkness both sides often identified friend and foe only by shouted words, bayonet and muzzle flash.
data: 人數方面，敬神黨的結集者據當時記錄約一百七十人，作戰時在場人數為一百七十四至二百餘人；官軍方面投入的是熊本鎮台步兵第十三連隊、砲兵第六大隊及縣警察部屯營巡查，總數無公開統計，但從傷亡名單看，陣亡將校與下級官員多達二十餘人。損失方面，敬神黨死者與自刃者合計一百二十四人，被俘約五十人，其中一部分被斬首；政府軍死亡約六十人，負傷約二百人——雙方加起來的死亡數接近一百八十人，集中在一夜之間，這在明治初年以來的城市騷亂中相當罕見。時間方面，戰鬥自十月二十四日深夜起，至二十五日清晨官軍奪回砲兵營為止，約數小時；縣令安岡良亮因傷於十月二十七日死亡，參事小關敬直延至翌年才去世。地理上，攻擊目標集中在熊本市區，離城牆不過數十分鐘步行路程，事後一百二十三名烈士合祀於城下黑髮的櫻山神社；一九二四年政府以名譽回復為由，向上述首領追贈正五位。唯一的通訊紀錄是那封十五個假名字的電報，成為日本電報文體的樣本。
dataEn: On numbers, the records put the Keishinto muster at about 170 men, with between 174 and a little over 200 present on the night. The government committed the Kumamoto garrison's 13th Infantry Regiment, the 6th Artillery Brigade and the district constables of the prefectural police; no overall figure was published, but the casualty lists show more than twenty officers and NCOs killed. In losses, the Keishinto lost 124 dead or self-inflicted deaths, and about fifty were captured, some of them beheaded; the government side lost about sixty dead and about two hundred wounded. Adding the two sides gives close to one hundred and eighty dead concentrated into a single night, which is remarkable for an urban rising in early Meiji. In time, the fighting lasted from late night on 24 October until the government retook the artillery camp on the morning of the 25th, a matter of hours; the prefect Yoshiaki Yasuoka died of his wounds on 27 October, and the councillor Naonobu Kozeki did not die until the following year. In geography, the targets lay in the Kumamoto town area, only a few minutes' walk from the castle walls; afterwards the 123 dead were jointly enshrined at Sakurayama Shrine in the Kurokami district below the castle. In 1924 the government, on the ground of rehabilitation of honour, conferred the posthumous rank of senior fifth rank on the leaders. The only surviving dispatch is the telegram of a mere fifteen katakana characters, which became a model of Japanese telegraphic style.
cause: 起因是明治政府對武士身分的一次清算。一八七一年廢藩置縣、一八七三年徵兵令與秩祿處分、一八七六年三月二十八日太政官布告第三十八號廢刀令，逐步抽走了武士的藩籍、俸祿與佩刀之權；廢刀令依據山縣有朋一八七五年十二月的建議，規定除大禮服著用者與在職軍人、警察官吏外不得帶刀，連平民在旅行、拜年、婚喪時佩帶小刀亦被禁止。熊本是廢刀令反對最盛的肥後熊本藩，藩內因教育方針分為三派：以朱子學為主的學校黨、橫井小楠所倡的實學黨，以及林櫻園一系以國學與神道立身的勤皇黨；勤皇黨中對明治政府強行推進警察制度、徵兵與文明開化不滿者，組成敬神愛護會的骨幹，名義上反對帶刀禁令，實際上已不滿於藩制被取消而藩士淪為無業之人。此前一八七四年的佐賀之亂已是同類事件的先聲。此次直接導火線是十月裡對私塾的取締以及鎮台司令官與縣令的連續遇襲，敬神黨遂決定以武裝起兵回應體制，結果演成一夜之間的攻城戰。
causeEn: The cause lay in a single sweeping liquidation of the samurai status by the Meiji government. The abolition of the han in 1871, the conscription ordinance and stipend measures of 1873, and the edict on banning swords, Taishofu hokoku dai sanjuhachi-go of 28 March 1876, took away in turn the samurai's domains, stipends and right to carry a blade. The sword edict rested on Yamagata Aritomo's recommendation of December 1875 and forbade carrying a sword except for wearers of formal court dress, soldiers on duty, police and officials, extending the ban to the small knives civilians had customarily worn when travelling, at New Year, at weddings and at funerals. Kumamoto was the heartland of opposition to the edict, in the Higo-Kumamoto domain, where the clan had split into three schools over educational policy: the school faction centred on Zhu Xi learning, the practical-learning faction advocated by Shonan Yokoi, and the loyalist faction built by Lin Sakuraen around kokugaku and Shinto. Among the loyalists, those most dissatisfied with the government's push for a police system, conscription and forced Westernisation formed the backbone of the Keishin Aigokai; nominally the movement opposed the sword ban, but in substance its members could no longer accept the cancellation of the domain system that left samurai without a livelihood. The Saga Rising of 1874 had already been a similar prologue. The immediate trigger was the suppression of the private schools in October and the successive attacks on the garrison commander and the prefect, and the Keishinto decided to answer the new order with arms, which produced a siege fought in a single night.
impact: 其一，暴露了當時日本軍制的脆弱：整個熊本鎮台因司令官與參謀長同日遇害而一度失去指揮，僥倖靠臨陣主將兒玉源太郎的機敏與步槍齊射的密度挽回。其二，把士族反亂推到頂點：同年十月二十七日秋月藩士起事、萩藩前原一誠起事接踵而至，一八七七年西鄉隆盛在薩摩舉兵，爆發規模遠勝此役的西南戰爭，最終以明治政府完勝、廢藩置縣與新軍制的全面落實收場；官軍在西南戰役中正是靠統一編制與後膛槍、砲的絕對數量壓倒薩軍，而加特林式多管機槍在那一役亦有實戰投入的記錄。其三，政治上的清算持續了半個世紀以上：一八八零年代起，櫻山神社建成，合祀林櫻園、宮部鼎藏、河上彥齋與一百二十三名烈士，熊本的烈士與遺物成為反骨精神的聖地；直到一九二四年，首領們才獲追贈正五位，三島由紀夫的《豐饒之海·奔馬》更把這段事寫成昭和之前反體制分子的精神源頭，讓它在文學中延續。
impactEn: First, it exposed the fragility of the military system of the time: the whole Kumamoto garrison lost command for a time because its commander and chief of staff were killed on the same night, and only the presence of mind of the field leader Gen'itaro Kodama and the sheer density of massed rifle fire saved the situation. Second, it drove the wave of samurai revolts to its height: the Akizuki rising of 27 October and the Hagi rising under Issei Maehara followed within days, and in 1877 Saigo Takamori raised his banner in Satsuma, the southwest war that followed dwarfing this episode and ending in the complete victory of the Meiji government and the full imposition of the new military system. In that southwest campaign the government army won precisely by uniform organisation and the absolute numbers of breechloading rifles and guns, and the Gatling gun too is recorded in action there. Third, the political reckoning ran for more than half a century: from the 1880s Sakurayama Shrine was built to enshrine Lin Sakuraen, Teibo Miya, Kawakami Kosai and the 123 dead, and the Kumamoto martyrs and their relics became a holy place for a spirit of defiance; only in 1924 were the leaders given the posthumous rank of senior fifth rank, and Mishima Yukio's Runmei, the second volume of The Sea of Fertility, turned the episode into the spiritual source of anti-system youth before the Showa era, carrying it on into literature.
result: 結果是政府軍的完勝。十月二十四日深夜起事，十月二十五日清晨官軍在兒玉源太郎指揮下攻入熊本城，收回砲兵營與武器庫，砲兵第六大隊與步兵第十三連隊恢復建制，屯營與縣廳的秩序重新建立。太田黑伴雄中彈重傷後在民家自刃，加屋霽堅、齋藤求三郎等人陣亡，其餘多數自刃或被俘，約五十人被捕，一部分被斬首；縣令安岡良亮於十月二十七日因傷死亡，參事小關敬直翌年不治。政府沒有因為事件而收回廢刀令，也沒有讓步，反而加速推進警察與徵兵制度：熊本鎮台司令官一職由兒玉源太郎接任，鎮西台所體系隨之整頓，使西鄉隆盛的薩軍在翌年舉兵時，熊本已是一座由新式軍制守備的城。事件最後成了明治政府把舊藩主與藩士編入新軍、並在西南戰爭中加以消耗的序曲，熊本從此成為西南戰爭的策源地。
resultEn: The result was a complete government victory. The rising began late on 24 October 1876, and on the morning of the 25th the government forces under Gen'itaro Kodama entered Kumamoto Castle, recovered the artillery camp and the arms store, and the 6th Artillery Brigade and the 13th Infantry Regiment were brought back into order, while the districts and the prefectural office regained their authority. Otaguro Tomoo, after being hit and grievously wounded, killed himself in a house; Kaya Harukata, Saito Kyuzabiro and others fell, most of the rest killed themselves or were taken, about fifty were captured and some of them beheaded. Prefect Yoshiaki Yasuoka died of his wounds on 27 October, and councillor Naonobu Kozeki died the following year. The government did not withdraw the sword edict or make any concession; instead it accelerated the police and conscription systems. The post of Kumamoto garrison commander passed to Gen'itaro Kodama, the Chinzei Depot was reorganised in step, and by the time Saigo Takamori's Satsuma forces rose in the following year, Kumamoto was a city defended under the new military system. The episode became the prelude to the Meiji government's absorption of the former domain lords and samurai into a new army, to be spent in the southwest war; Kumamoto had become the place from which the southwest war would spring.
